I light a few candles, find a class, let the teacher set the vibe and go on a necessary journey to re center myself.

Beginner classes all are over an hour long. For me it’s simply too long and I want flexibility in when and where I do them. In another app I do the scheduling and time up front and can choose in the app if I want yin, restorative, gentle, hatha and the level. Plus I choose an amount of time that works for me. Your app simply does not provide a level of flexibility for a beginner class tailored to what I want and need. Secondly the app does not record the sessions in Apple health. I like looking at my day of walking, mindfulness in the app. It’s a central guideline of my day. Finally there is no real scheduling or mentoring in the app. I would like to chart my own course and decide to do shorter classes as I want at a beginner level that fit my needs. I’ve basically given up on the app and will just take the hit for the subscription and move to the down dog app. It does the basic beginner things I want. I can choose everything up front and it logs the workout.

I think the app has a long way to go for beginners like me.

reviews.text:
Living again. I have been doing the beginning classes by Jackie Casal Mahrou along with the stretching series for men by Robert Sidoti since January and because I have severe osteoarthritis in both knees, (stage III), and the stretching is the first thing I must do each morning before I can move in my day. It has improved my overall well-being to the point that if I have to miss a morning and I do not have bad swelling when I wake, I can actually skip a morning of working out in my hot tub. This is something I could not do for three years before. Heat was always necessary first thing in the morning just to get moving. Jackie’s classes have helped my balance and strength and endurance so much that I have all but put away my walker! I can volunteer, shop, walk my dogs, do years work and I have even been able to keep pace walking with my 24 year old daughter while walking her dog and she’s in excellent shape. 

Robert’s stretching class doesn’t require me to stand which is one reason I can do it first thing. My knees are most swollen when I wake and therefore in the most pain, but I must move to get going. So his stretches are the ideal answer for me allowing me to be on my back and warm up my muscles. Jackie’s classes are all fantastic as they move at a pace slow enough but building upon the last skill set which allows me to grow in flexibility and learn to trust that my body can remember to let go of being so stiff.

I decided to try something new mostly due to my daughter’s wedding along with my constant seeking anything to relieve pain but when I had tried yoga in the past instructors moved between positions too quickly. I could never transition fast enough and I felt foolish trying to keep up with everyone. So I left the room.

The beginning classes and stretching ones are paced perfectly for me. I haven’t ever had to stop or even pause them. I can complete every class and feel stronger and more balanced with every class I complete. I spend two weeks on each class and move onto the next one. My Mom is a physical therapist and she even remarked that she thought my posture seemed improved and I do actually feel taller. I know I am moving faster and surer and the inches lost mean little to me compared to less pain and more security in my movements and the fact that I am likely to be dancing at my daughter’s wedding in June! It feels so good to feel my age rather than like I’m much older. I have worked out consistently walking in my hot tub (it has a treadmill in it) for 3 years since my last knee surgery in 2016 and did not receive the same level of overall benefit from that tub as I have from regular yoga. I am truly stunned. I’m only 48 and want to enjoy so much more and doing yoga has been the first activity that has made me believe the flexibility over time might actually be something that can impact my overall experience of life enough to make me feel warmer inside and less like I am this disease of osteoarthritis. And more like I am just someone who copes with bouts of osteoarthritis on occasion.

So thank you for making stretching exercises that don’t stand the entire time. And beginning exercise classes that move and transition slowly enough for a beginner to follow. It feels so good to warm up and move through life again. I think Robert and Jackie have voices like angels!

Sincerely,
Christy Hall
